title: The Camel That Refused to Turn Right (PT)
summary: A stubborn courtier refuses to change his outdated administrative methods. Birbal uses a trained camel to satirize stubborn conservatism. [PT]
full_text:
A senior imperial minister named Khwaja Nizamuddin was notoriously obstinate. He insisted on maintaining fifty-year-old taxation procedures that were cumbersome, costly, and caused immense delays in trade. When Birbal proposed modernizing the trade registries, the old minister argued: 'Our ancestors did it this way! To change our direction is a betrayal of tradition!'

Akbar was hesitant to overrule the elder minister.

The next morning, Birbal invited Akbar and Khwaja Nizamuddin to take a ride through the narrow streets of the old city of Agra. Birbal provided the old minister with a magnificent royal camel from the desert provinces.

As they rode down a narrow alleyway, they approached a sharp right turn that led to the grand bazaar.

Khwaja Nizamuddin pulled the right rein. The camel refused to turn right! It shook its head, snorted, and continued marching straight ahead toward a high brick dead-end wall!

The minister yanked the rein with all his might: 'Turn right, you stupid beast! The road is to the right!'

The camel ignored the command and planted its nose firmly against the solid brick wall, refusing to budge.

'Why will this cursed camel not turn right?' the minister shouted in frustration.

Birbal rode up with a pleasant smile:

'Khwaja Sahib, you should praise this noble camel! You see, its grandfather and great-grandfather were desert camels who always walked in a straight line across the dunes!

'This camel is fiercely loyal to its ancient traditions! It believes that turning right is a dangerous novelty, so it insists on marching straight into a brick wall rather than adapting to the new turn of the road!'

Akbar burst into hearty laughter, while Khwaja Nizamuddin blushed deeply, recognizing his own stubbornness in the obstinate beast.

The old minister yielded with a good-natured smile: 'I understand your sermon, Birbal! If an empire refuses to turn when the road turns, it will smash its head against the wall of history!'

With the minister's consent, the administrative reforms were implemented smoothly, speeding up commerce across the empire.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
